races.name: Welcome To The Perth Festival Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Off The Jury
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the pace scenario but 67 days off and wind operations create legitimate fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time to make it 0-12 under rules but leading claims judged on peak efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in Haydock handicap in February to make it 0-12 under rules; had wind operations before and after that latest run; arrives with something to prove but he has lots of good placed form and is a leading contender if back on song; the tongue-tie adopted last time is left off.

runners_data.name: Holy Joe
runners_data.note: Unraced newcomer from Gordon Elliott's yard with half-brother to 2m4f hurdle winner, complete unknown on going
runners_data.comment: Top Irish trainer also runs the experienced Newbrook Diamond; check the betting on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Sixth foal; half-brother to winners Miss Aloud (2m4f hurdle for these connections; RPR 118) and Oak Bluffs (7f-1m4f Flat); dam unraced; no surprise to see a big run on debut; top Irish trainer also runs the experienced Newbrook Diamond and the betting could be informative.

runners_data.name: Expensive Emotion
runners_data.note: Point winner stepping up to rules racing, new trainer Adrian Keatley having excellent season but another going unknown
runners_data.comment: Bought for £40,000 after point win; new trainer is having an excellent season
runners_data.spotlight: Won Irish mares' maiden point (3m, yielding to soft) last November on her second start and sold for £40,000 in December; new trainer is having an excellent season and she could have a part to play on rules debut.

runners_data.name: Gee Force Flyer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner ideally placed to track Newbrook Diamond, consistent soft ground form gives confidence in conditions
runners_data.comment: Third of 17 in the competitive EBF Final at Sandown and strong claims on the back of that
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who has finished in the first three on all four hurdle starts (soft/good to soft), most recently third on handicap debut in the competitive EBF Final at Sandown (2m4f); strong claims on the back of that.

runners_data.name: Newbrook Diamond
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader will get uncontested advantage, but 0-6 over hurdles record despite four places raises questions
runners_data.comment: 0-6 over hurdles and below par latest, but placed 4 times and major player if back to best
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who made it 0-6 over hurdles when 26l seventh of 25 at Fairyhouse recently in first-time blinkers (retained); however, he's been placed four times in this sphere and will be a major player for his top Irish trainer if back to his best this afternoon.

runners_data.name: Minutes To Spare
runners_data.note: Non-runner, hold-up style would have suited the pace but beaten 16 lengths on debut at Ayr
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten on last month's debut but useful pedigree and open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten at 15-2 on last month's debut in a maiden hurdle at Ayr (2m, soft); however, this 90,000euros purchase has a useful pedigree and may be able to take a sizeable step forward for his in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Heffalump
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from in-form Donald McCain yard, 143 days off since Carlisle bumper but has had wind surgery
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to useful Kiltealy Briggs but tailed off on sole bumper start; wind op since
runners_data.spotlight: From in-form yard and he's a half-brother to the useful Kiltealy Briggs; he's had wind surgery since his debut in a Carlisle bumper (2m1f, soft) last November but was tailed off at 16-1 and a transformation is needed.

runners_data.name: Prince Phil
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but pulled up on both hurdle starts, headgear change to hood suggests connections still searching for improvement
runners_data.comment: Fairly encouraging fifth in sole bumper but pulled up/tailed off on both hurdle starts
runners_data.spotlight: Fairly encouraging fifth at Kelso in February in his sole bumper but pulled up/tailed off at triple-figure odds on both hurdle starts.

runners_data.name: Eagle's Cairn
runners_data.note: Hold-up style fits race shape but three consecutive pull-ups over hurdles make him hard to trust
runners_data.comment: Pulled up on his last three starts and he would be a surprise winner
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some ability in a bumper and on hurdle debut but pulled up over hurdles on his last three starts and he would be a surprise winner.

runners_data.name: Run Baby Run
runners_data.note: Extreme hold-up runner but 200-1 for all five starts and pulled up every time tells the story
runners_data.comment: 200-1 or bigger for all five runs; pulled up/tailed off each time
runners_data.spotlight: 200-1 or bigger for all five runs; pulled up/tailed off each time.

races.paceDynamic: Newbrook Diamond is the only confirmed front runner and will set an uncontested lead from the start. With Gee Force Flyer likely to track him in second, the pace will be moderate and sustainable through the early stages. The lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a tactical affair where stamina and jumping efficiency become paramount over the extended 2m4f trip. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay the trip and produce a sustained finish, as the leaders will have plenty left for a genuine gallop from the final flight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace allows closers to conserve energy and unleash late runs
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead means Newbrook Diamond and Gee Force Flyer will still be there turning for home but vulnerable to stronger stayers. Hold-up horses with proven stamina will have the tactical advantage to pick them off in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Hold On
scenarios.trigger: If Newbrook Diamond and Gee Force Flyer have enough left after the moderate early gallop
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure means both leaders retain enough energy to resist the late challenge. Their established jumping rhythm and forward position prove decisive over this stamina-testing distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Maiden Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the experienced runners fail to capitalise and one of the newcomers shows untapped ability
scenarios.body: The tactical nature of the race allows an improving type to slip through and demonstrate superior natural ability. Holy Joe or Expensive Emotion could surprise if their point form translates effectively to rules racing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Newbrook Diamond stops quickly and Gee Force Flyer also fades dramatically in the straight
scenarios.body: The absence of any genuine pace-setter creates a crawling finish where any horse with a gear change can win. Even the outsiders get a chance in what becomes a sprint finish from the last flight.

watchPoints.text: Newbrook Diamond could stop quickly if his 0-6 hurdles record reflects a genuine stamina limitation at this trip
Off The Jury needs monitoring for wind issues given his pulled-up effort at Haydock and subsequent operations
Holy Joe and Expensive Emotion deserve respect as unraced newcomers from quality connections despite going concerns
Gee Force Flyer's consistent soft ground placings make him the most reliable each-way option in this weak maiden
Minutes To Spare is a non-runner which removes one potential hold-up challenger from the scenario mix

races.name: Balnakeilly Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Barlovento
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario, though 39 days off and recent poor form at higher grades are concerns.
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten on last two starts but in tougher races; he remains one to be interested in
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten on last two starts but those were Class 2 contests at Cheltenham and Kempton and this is a drop back in grade; this lightly raced 7yo had previously made a promising start to his chasing career, including a 2m4f win at Kempton, and he remains one to be interested in.

runners_data.name: King Roly
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent course record (2 wins from 2 starts) but 193-day absence raises fitness questions.
runners_data.comment: Has a very solid record here and could play a leading role if fully tuned up after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Made a good start to his chasing career last year, winning three times between May and September (2m3f/2m4f, good), with two of them over C&D; also effective on good to soft, unproven on softer; he has a very solid record here and could play a leading role if fully tuned up after a break.

runners_data.name: Great Pepper
runners_data.note: Forward-going type who showed promise when second at Ayr but pulled up last time and trainer is cold.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Ayr in January but pulled up at Carlisle since and needs to bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 8yo who was runner-up at Ayr (2m, soft) in January when dropped back in trip on his second chase start; however, pulled up at Carlisle (2m, good to soft) since, which severely dents confidence in his claims today, and the step up in distance may not be ideal.

runners_data.name: Find A Fortune
runners_data.note: Needs to improve on recent chase debuts but prominent style and Gordon Elliott training angle provide hope.
runners_data.comment: Improvement needed on third chase start but yard's horses always worth a second look here
runners_data.spotlight: 9yo who is lightly raced for his age; he needs to produce more than he managed at Leopardstown and Downpatrick last month on his first two chase starts but he wears first-time headgear today and Gordon Elliott's horses are always well worth a second look at Perth; could have a big say.

runners_data.name: Walking On A Dream
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner whose style creates the pace but 5lb claiming jockey helps his chances of lasting home.

runners_data.name: Karafon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose runner-up effort at Ayr shows ability but three poor runs since suggest he's regressing.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Ayr in January but three lesser efforts have followed; has to raise his game
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up when back over fences at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in January and this 6yo is of interest on that form; however, three lesser performances have followed and he needs to raise his game if he's to win this.

runners_data.name: Wolfburg
runners_data.note: Non-runner originally but fresh off Monday's win at Kelso with cheekpieces helping his recent resurgence.
runners_data.comment: 3-5 since cheekpieces went on, the latest win on Monday; 7lb penalty might not stop him
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins (2m3f-2m7f, soft-good) from his five starts since these cheekpieces went on, the latest in gutsy fashion at Kelso on Monday when clear with a rejuvenated runner-up; a 7lb penalty might not stop this progressive 7yo if today's assignment doesn't come too soon.

runners_data.name: It's Hard To Know
runners_data.note: Fellow pace-setter returning after 137 days off which makes fitness a major question mark.
runners_data.comment: Just one run this season, when soundly beaten on chase debut, but he's not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Point (3m, soft to heavy) and two-time novice hurdle (2m3f/2m4f, good/good to soft) winner; he's run just once this season, when 14l fourth of six on chase debut at Aintree (2m4f, soft) in December; however, he remains very lightly raced and is certainly not written off today.

races.paceDynamic: It's Hard To Know and Walking On A Dream will force an honest early pace with both confirmed front-runners likely to contest the lead from flagfall. The small field of eight runners means there won't be excessive pressure, allowing these leaders to dictate a solid but not punishing gallop through the first mile. King Roly and Great Pepper sitting prominent will keep them honest without creating a collapse scenario. This setup creates a genuine test of stamina over the final 4-5 furlongs, clearly favouring hold-up horses like Barlovento, Karafon, and Wolfburg who can produce finishing kicks when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners maintain their honest pace throughout the race.
scenarios.body: The leaders will weaken in the final half-mile, allowing closers with tactical speed to sweep past in the closing stages. Horses held up off the pace will have the freshest finishing kick when it matters most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker strikes
scenarios.trigger: If King Roly or Great Pepper can sit the perfect trip just behind the leaders.
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners will have the ideal position to strike when the leaders tire but before the hold-up horses fully wind up. Their forward position gives them first run on the field when the race develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner stays strong
scenarios.trigger: If Walking On A Dream gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home.
scenarios.body: The leader will have enough left in the tank to repel late challenges, especially with the jockey's 5lb claim reducing the burden. The honest pace won't be strong enough to completely drain the leader's stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early or make jumping errors.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish with all runners bunched together at the last fence. Any horse with a turn of foot regardless of position could capitalize on the tactical chaos.

watchPoints.text: It's Hard To Know may not be race-fit after 137 days off and could fold quickly if pressed by Walking On A Dream early.
King Roly's fitness after 193-day layoff is crucial - any signs of rustiness in the paddock would be significant.
Great Pepper's jumping needs monitoring as he pulled up last time and any early mistakes could end hopes.
Walking On A Dream's 5lb claimer Jack Power must not let the pace become too strong in the opening mile.
Wolfburg's late entry and quick turnaround from Monday's Kelso win - watch for any signs of hard race effects.

races.name: British EBF Gold Castle 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: No Drama This End
runners_data.note: Front runner with class edge (OR 144) gets tactical advantage but hasn't raced for 42 days and was disappointing last time at Cheltenham
runners_data.comment: Grade 1 winner; disappointing favourite at Cheltenham but the one to beat if back to best
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 3-3 over hurdles (2m5f/2m4f, soft/good) in ready fashion in the Grade 1 Challow at Newbury in December; very disappointing favourite in the Turners at the Cheltenham Festival, even allowing for what went wrong at the start, but he's the one to beat today if back to his best; promises to be suited by the step up in trip (dam won 3m French Grade 1).

runners_data.name: Kazansky
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from Gordon Elliott stable with solid Grade race form, ideally placed to track the leader and pounce
runners_data.comment: Grade 2 winner; pulled up at Cheltenham but one to be interested in back in calmer waters
runners_data.spotlight: Won Grade 2 novice hurdle at Limerick (2m7f, heavy) in December and 8l second in Grade 1 at Leopardstown (2m6f, heavy) in February; pulled up at 25-1 in the Albert Bartlett at Cheltenham (3m, soft) last month but back in calmer waters today and he's one to be interested in given his previous promise.

runners_data.name: Sogna In Grande
runners_data.note: Perfect record over hurdles (2-2) suggests untapped potential, but hold-up style needs pace to develop
runners_data.comment: 2-2 over hurdles; others have stronger form but remains to be seen where limitations lie
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who is 2-2 over hurdles following novice wins at Warwick (2m5f, soft) and Wincanton (2m5f, good); others have more substance to their form but he did it easily last time and it remains to be seen where his limitations lie.

runners_data.name: Blue Run
runners_data.comment: Convincing win at Southwell in February and could have lots more to offer for top trainer
runners_data.spotlight: Left December's debut run (2m5f, good to soft) well behind to win in good style at Southwell (2m4f, soft) in February; faces a much higher calibre of opponent today but he could have lots more to offer for his top trainer.

runners_data.name: Tormund Giantsbane
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was well beaten by No Drama This End previously but showed improvement when winning last time
runners_data.comment: No match for No Drama This End at Sandown but he's improved since; can go well
runners_data.spotlight: No match for the winner No Drama This End when 12l fourth of five in Grade 2 at Sandown (2m4f, soft) in December; however, he showed improved form when easily making all in Doncaster novice (3m, good to soft) in February and can give a good account in his rematch; has also won on soft.

runners_data.name: Sept Etoiles
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse with only four career starts, most recent win suggests upward trajectory but needs strong pace
runners_data.comment: Impressive in big-field handicap at Fairyhouse this month; respected despite tougher task
runners_data.spotlight: 5yo who has raced four times, all over hurdles, and he was winning for a second time when powering clear in a big-field handicap at Fairyhouse (3m, yielding to soft) this month; today is a tougher test of his credentials but he was impressive last time and could be up to the task.

races.paceDynamic: No Drama This End and Blue Run are the confirmed front runners, but with Blue Run a non-runner, No Drama This End will face less early pressure and can dictate terms from the front. The pace-setters Kazansky (prominent) and potentially Sogna In Grande will track the leader, but this small field creates a risk of steady fractions early before quickening. The hold-up horses Tormund Giantsbane and Sept Etoiles will be relying on the pace collapsing, but with only one natural leader remaining, this race shape strongly favours those who can travel kindly in the first three positions and have the class to sustain their effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Classy Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If No Drama This End gets an uncontested lead and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: The Paul Nicholls runner can use his superior class rating (OR 144) to dictate fractions and kick clear when it matters. His three hurdle wins have all come from prominent positions and this tactical advantage could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes steady early and creates a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace pressure allows Tormund Giantsbane or Sept Etoiles to get into contention and unleash their finishing kicks. Both have shown they can quicken off slower gallops and benefit from tactical racing.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Improving Type Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Sogna In Grande or unexposed runners step forward significantly
scenarios.body: The Kim Bailey runner is unbeaten over hurdles (2-2) and could have more improvement than the others realize. His hold-up style works if he gets the right pace setup and his trainers are in good form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If No Drama This End goes too fast early trying to dominate or ties up
scenarios.body: The leader could pay for doing too much work alone up front, allowing any of the closers to pick up the pieces. This would particularly suit Kazansky who can travel prominently without leading.

watchPoints.text: No Drama This End could get an easy lead with Blue Run withdrawn - watch if he can dictate his preferred fractions
Kazansky has pulled up before and his fitness after 40 days absence needs monitoring early in the race
Sogna In Grande is trained by Kim Bailey & Mat Nicholls partnership who have limited runners but decent strike rate
The pace could go steady early with only one natural front runner - this would disadvantage the hold-up horses
Tormund Giantsbane was 12 lengths behind No Drama This End when they met at Sandown in December

races.name: Fair Maid Of Perth Mares' Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Apple Away
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 171-day break but won this race in 2022 on similar soft ground
runners_data.comment: Won this two years ago; just one run this season (November) but can give a good account
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent sort who won this two years ago (soft); Panic Attack has better form and she's run just once this season, but that was a solid effort when third of five at Carlisle in November over an inadequate 2m4f (good to soft), and she can give a good account.

runners_data.name: Panic Attack
runners_data.note: Natural leader with superior class but only 11 days since Grand National fall which raises fitness questions
runners_data.comment: Early exit in Grand National 11 days ago; leading claims on the rest of her form this term
runners_data.spotlight: Ran in the Grand National 11 days ago, badly hampered at the second fence and falling at the third; won two high-profile handicaps last November before Listed win at Newbury and the drop back to 2m4f didn't appear ideal at the Cheltenham Festival; leading claims if none the worse for last time.

runners_data.name: Shecouldbeanything
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare carrying headgear changes but pulled up in Irish National just 16 days ago
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in recent Irish National but running well in January and could bounce back today
runners_data.spotlight: She'll find it hard to beat a peak-form Panic Attack and she was pulled up in the Irish National 16 days ago; however, she was running well in January, in a Grade 2 mares' chase at Fairyhouse (2m6f, yielding) and the Thyestes Handicap at Gowran Park (3m1f, heavy; albeit no match for the first two); no surprise if she bounces back with a good performance today.

runners_data.name: Ruby Island
runners_data.note: Progressive chaser stepping up significantly in class but open to further improvement at 9 years old
runners_data.comment: Progressive during this first chasing campaign but further improvement is needed
runners_data.spotlight: 9yo who has been progressive during this first chasing campaign, winning twice (2m/2m4f, soft/good to soft); she's open to further improvement but it's necessary now back up in grade, and she needs to prove her stamina; soundly beaten over hurdles on sole previous run in these cheekpieces.

races.paceDynamic: Panic Attack will likely lead or share the pace with Apple Away, both prominent runners who can dictate from the front. With only four runners and no confirmed hold-up specialists, the early pace should be genuine but not suicidal over this 3m trip. Shecouldbeanything and Ruby Island will need to track the leaders and hope for a strong finish. This shape clearly favours the prominent runners who can control the tempo and kick for home when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Panic Attack Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Panic Attack recovers fully from Grand National exertions and dictates the pace
scenarios.body: The 10-year-old uses superior class (OR 147) to dominate from the front, with Apple Away struggling to match the relentless gallop. Recent Listed winner proves too strong in the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Apple Away Redemption
scenarios.trigger: If Apple Away finds her 2022 winning form and Panic Attack shows fatigue effects
scenarios.body: The former winner uses course knowledge and soft ground expertise to outlast a below-par Panic Attack in a tactical battle. Lucinda Russell's mare peaks at the right moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ruby Island Progression
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and Ruby Island's stamina kicks in late
scenarios.body: The improving chaser benefits from a slow-run race that becomes a sprint finish, using her progressive profile to outfinish tiring leaders. Nicky Richards' timing proves perfect.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shecouldbeanything Bounce
scenarios.trigger: If Gordon Elliott's mare shows no ill-effects from Irish National pull-up
scenarios.body: The hold-up performer finds the steady pace ideal for a late charge, overcoming recent disappointment with a trademark finish. Class tells in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Panic Attack showing any signs of the Grand National taking its toll in the early stages
Apple Away's jumping rhythm after such a long layoff period
Ruby Island's ability to cope with this significant step up in grade
Shecouldbeanything's early enthusiasm given recent headgear addition
The pace development with only four runners and potential for tactical riding

races.name: Bedmax Capercaillie Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Fringill Dike
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who hasn't won since Newton Abbot but the 185-day break could have refreshed him for this easier assignment.
runners_data.comment: Rather lost his way; 185-day break may help but forecast soft ground also raises doubts
runners_data.spotlight: Won four of his first five completed starts over fences (2023/24) but just one success since, a Newton Abbot handicap, and he wasn't finishing his races off last year; 185-day break may have helped but this forecast soft ground raises further doubts.

runners_data.name: Jigoro
runners_data.note: Will make the running but his modest TopSpeed figure suggests he's vulnerable if the pace quickens significantly.
runners_data.comment: 31P in handicap chases, the pulled up probably best ignored; unexposed and needs respect
runners_data.spotlight: Blinkered first time when third of 14 on his handicap debut in this sphere at Thurles (2m5f, yielding) in January and off the mark over fences when landing fairly valuable event at Gowran (2m, heavy) last month; 22-1 and pulled up in Listed novice handicap last time but that had the makings of a warm event and he needs respecting.

runners_data.name: Heltenham
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who excels at this trip and won at this meeting last year, making him the form horse to beat.
runners_data.comment: Mark and drop in trip ask a question but he's impossible to rule out
runners_data.spotlight: All chase wins around 2m4f, including win at this meeting last year; Newbury specialist who landed fourth win at that track when bagging valuable handicap for second time on penultimate start; never won off a mark this high and drop back down to 2m also asks a question but he's impossible to rule out.

runners_data.name: Aeros Luck
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying bottom weight with an in-form trainer whose 4/11 record demands respect.
runners_data.comment: February's close second on penultimate start was a creditable effort; stable in fine form
runners_data.spotlight: Another ex-Gavin Cromwell inmate who secured narrow win over fences at Punchestown (2m, good to yielding) in June; 0-5 for this yard but February's close second of five at Musselburgh (2m, good to soft) on penultimate start was a creditable effort; stable in fine form.

runners_data.name: Coup De Coeur
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who can be erratic at his fences but showed progressive form when winning at Sedgefield in February.
runners_data.comment: Good second in fairly valuable series final (2m, good to soft) one month ago; progressive
runners_data.spotlight: Can be hit and miss in the jumping department but his profile over fences is generally progressive and he backed up February's Sedgefield romp with good second in fairly valuable series final at Carlisle (also 2m, good to soft) one month ago; respected.

runners_data.name: Sunnyvilla
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner who has won twice with give in the ground for current connections and handles soft conditions well.
runners_data.comment: Veteran but 2-6 for this yard and 2m4f a plausible excuse last time; needs consideration
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran of the field but he won over 2m with plenty of give underfoot on first and fifth races for this yard, latterly at Uttoxeter in January on penultimate start; 2m4f a plausible excuse last time and he needs consideration.

runners_data.name: The Other Mozzie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making stable debut for L J Morgan after disappointing recent efforts, wearing a visor for the first time.
runners_data.comment: Yard debut ignored; on last winning mark with first-time visor & Harry Cobden taking over
runners_data.spotlight: Three chase wins for Gavin Cromwell included comfortable win in good event at Ayr (2m, good to soft) one year ago; fluffed the start on stable debut in Cheltenham's Grand Annual but had yet to be asked for his effort when falling three out last month; now back down to that Ayr mark, while the first-time visor and booking of Harry Cobden are other points of interest.

races.paceDynamic: Jigoro will take them along at a reasonable clip with Fringill Dike, Aeros Luck and Sunnyvilla tracking close behind in the early stages. The pace won't be demanding given limited early speed, allowing the hold-up horses Heltenham, Coup De Coeur and The Other Mozzie to settle comfortably in behind. This modest gallop will set up a sprint finish over the final 3-4 furlongs where positioning and stamina reserves become crucial. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can quicken late, disadvantaging those who need a strong pace to soften up front-runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Jigoro sets only a moderate pace and the field stays bunched
scenarios.body: The race becomes a 2-furlong dash where class and finishing kick matter most. Hold-up horses with proven acceleration like Heltenham and Coup De Coeur can unleash their finishing speed from ideal positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Win
scenarios.trigger: If Fringill Dike or Aeros Luck press Jigoro early and increase the tempo
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches the field and favours those tracking the leaders who can inherit the race. Prominent racers avoid traffic problems and can strike approaching the final fence when leaders tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a crawl
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the home turn where only horses with explosive acceleration can win. Heltenham's 2m4f pedigree and The Other Mozzie's class become decisive factors in a slowly-run contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Jigoro gets an uncontested lead and no one pressures
scenarios.body: The Gordon Elliott-trained gelding can dictate terms completely and prove hard to peg back. His recent form suggests he has the stamina to maintain his advantage if allowed easy sectionals throughout.

watchPoints.text: Heltenham jumping the final fence in front as his hold-up style and class advantage make him formidable in a finish

races.paceDynamic: Atlantic City looks the only natural pace-setter in this small field of seven, giving her a comfortable lead without pressure from the start. With six hold-up horses including Flying Fortune, Fresh As A Daisy, and Spit Spot all likely to be held up, this creates a stop-start rhythm with a moderate gallop for most of the journey. The lack of pace pressure means Atlantic City can dictate terms and potentially steal a march, while the hold-up brigade may find themselves with too much to do if she gets away with soft fractions. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and early pace-setters who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Atlantic City Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Atlantic City gets uncontested fractions and kicks for home early enough
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows her to build an unassailable lead while the hold-up horses get in each other's way. Her recent Haydock second shows she has the ability, and with tactical advantage she can outrun her OR of 105.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Tells Late
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses can organize themselves and mount a coordinated challenge
scenarios.body: Flying Fortune's superior class (OR 122) and four-race winning streak in 2024 tells, despite her recent poor form. The soft ground suits her perfectly and she gets a strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Course Specialist Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Spit Spot reproduces her course form with the addition of cheekpieces
scenarios.body: Her two wins here last autumn on similar ground give her a significant edge, and the headgear change could spark improvement. Just An Artist's course win also comes into play as the locals benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Henderson Filly Improves
scenarios.trigger: If Fresh As A Daisy builds on her recent Newbury effort despite the poor result
scenarios.body: The Nicky Henderson factor and her previous 2m4f win suggest she's better than her handicap debut showed. The softer ground and more suitable pace scenario could unlock her potential.

races.paceDynamic: Rioja Alta will likely set the pace from the front with limited pressure, as most rivals prefer to sit behind or hold up positions. Jeteye and Coylton King may track the leader in prominent positions, but the majority of this field are hold-up horses including Bollin Matilda, Follow Charlie, and Suspected. The soft ground and 3-mile trip will create a searching test of stamina, with the pace likely to be steady early before quickening significantly from the back straight. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can establish good positions early and avoid traffic problems that could plague the large contingent of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Rioja Alta gets an uncontested lead and maintains a steady gallop...
scenarios.body: The pace will be manageable early allowing her to conserve energy for a strong finish, with the hold-up horses struggling to make up ground on the soft surface. Her proven form on similar conditions and ability to dictate terms makes her very dangerous.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Jeteye or Coylton King can track the pace and time their challenge perfectly...
scenarios.body: They can get first run on the leader while the hold-up horses are still making their move from the rear. The soft ground will make it difficult for back-markers to close the gap once these prominent runners establish a lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too strong or the front-runners tire dramatically...
scenarios.body: Bollin Matilda or Follow Charlie could benefit from a truly-run race where stamina becomes the deciding factor. However, they need significant pace collapse and perfect positioning from their amateur jockeys.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Rioja Alta goes too fast early or gets pressured by the prominent racers...
scenarios.body: The race could fall apart in the final mile allowing a closer like Pure Sirloin to pick up the pieces. This requires multiple front-runners to make tactical errors and ideal splits for the hold-up horses.

races.paceDynamic: Kells Priory will likely lead with Maillot Blanc, Ebselysees, Palm Beach and Blue Indigo up prominent, creating a solid gallop but nothing savage over this 3m trip on soft ground. The hold-up brigade of Shighness, Maura Jeanne, Monsieur Le Fuzz, Ck O'Mara, Am I Bovvered and Roi Du Roume will track behind in what should be a truly-run staying test. With amateur jockeys aboard and the testing conditions, the pace will be honest rather than frantic, allowing patient tactics to prosper. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay every yard and finish with a sustained challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves testing but not breakneck over 3m on soft ground with amateur riders settling their mounts
scenarios.body: The prominent group will weaken in the final half-mile as the stamina test bites, allowing the patient hold-up performers to sweep past with superior fitness and tactical positioning. Horses like Shighness, Maura Jeanne and Monsieur Le Fuzz have proven 3m+ form and will benefit from being delivered late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Kells Priory and Maillot Blanc maintain a strong gallop and both stay the trip well
scenarios.body: These two will dominate from the front with their superior class showing through, potentially running the hold-up horses out of it if they can maintain their stamina. Both have solid form at the trip and won't mind the conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lesser-rated horses finds significant improvement stepping up to 3m in these testing conditions
scenarios.body: The pace will suit an unexposed type who has been crying out for this distance, with the soft ground helping their stamina reserves. Am I Bovvered or Blue Indigo could be the beneficiaries of a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Class Horse Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Kells Priory is allowed an easy lead and amateur jockey tactics play into his hands
scenarios.body: The ex-Irish performer will use his superior class rating to build an unassailable advantage, with the chasing pack leaving their runs too late on the testing surface. His recent Wincanton fourth suggests he's ready to strike.

watchPoints.text: Kells Priory getting too soft a lead early - amateur jockeys may not press him and allow him to control the race
Shighness and Maura Jeanne getting too far back - both need to be positioned to strike in the final mile
Palm Beach's jumping after two recent falls - any early mistakes will end her chances immediately

First-time headgear on Blue Indigo and blinkers first time on Shighness potentially improving performance
